name: ProtoBindingRulesForm
description: Per-connection protobuf topic-binding rules: add, edit, reorder, delete, and test topic matches against loaded message types.

props.name: rules
props.description: ProtoBindingRuleView[] in priority order; the topmost wins ties on an equally specific filter.

props.name: descriptorNames
props.description: Full message-type names available from the loaded proto registry.

props.name: status
props.description: loadError/dirMissing/folderNotFound summary. dirMissing (no dir configured) picks the empty-state copy; loadError and folderNotFound gate the stale-type warning on rows. The section's own status line (file/type counts) is rendered by the container above this component and isn't passed down.

props.name: connected
props.description: Shows 'Bindings stay editable while connected and apply to new messages.' when true, so the section doesn't read as locked under the dialog's locked-while-connected notice.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: May return a promise; a rejection is shown inline instead of being swallowed.

props.name: onUpdate
props.description: May return a promise; a rejection is shown inline instead of being swallowed.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: May return a promise; a rejection is shown inline instead of being swallowed.

props.name: onMove
props.description: May return a promise; a rejection is shown inline instead of being swallowed.

notes: Props-only render (no store reads, no bindings imports); the ProtoSection container owns bindings calls, rule CRUD, and ProtoStateChanged refetch. The type picker lives in the sibling ProtoTypePicker component (shared by committed rows and the draft row); it isn't listed in dependencies[] because both are tier 'component' and the validator only allows component -> primitive edges. Extracting a shared SearchableDropdownMenu primitive across components is a good follow-up (explicitly a v1 non-goal in the per-topic-protobuf design doc). Row notes are a single derived array (rowNotes) with precedence validation error > failed save > duplicate filter > stale type; the first two redden the input, only validation blocks the commit, the rest are amber. A failed onUpdate keeps the row's edit dirty (so a refresh can't replace the unsaved text and the next edit or blur retries) and shows 'Could not save: <error>' on the row; a failed onDelete/onMove shows under the list, a failed onAdd under the draft. Picking a type in the draft row marks the filter touched, so an empty or invalid filter shows its error then; opening the picker alone doesn't. Reorder buttons carry aria-labels ('Move up', 'Move down') via IconButton's ariaLabel.
